_README: Problems in the ENGLISH source texts, found while the worksheets were machine-translated (November 2026) and checked against the English. Fix them in the partner's Word document; the reader picks the change up on the next 'node tools/reader.mjs folder'. Set "status" to "fixed" when done. Shown on translations/issues.html.

types.error: Wrong fact, wrong calculation or text cut off
types.copy: Copied from another worksheet by mistake
types.consistency: Two places in the worksheet disagree
types.suggestion: Not wrong, but worth a look

issues.problem: Learning outcome stops in the middle of the sentence.
issues.fix: Finish the sentence, e.g. “Students evaluate the environmental impact of …”.

issues.problem: “Did you know?” box about a clothesline or drying rack — this belongs to the washing machine/dryer worksheet, not dishwashers.
issues.fix: Replace with a dishwasher fact or remove.

issues.problem: Water price is 0.002 €/l in the resources line and the worked example (t3f4c69c1, tb36ad0e4) but 0.003 €/l in Activity 1 and the later question.
issues.fix: Use one price everywhere (or say clearly that Activity 1 uses a different price).

issues.problem: Clothesline / drying rack line copied from the washing worksheet; the hair dryer worksheet already has its own “air-drying uses 0 kWh” fact.
issues.fix: Remove the clothesline line.

issues.problem: Says that since 2021 personal care appliances over 100 W must carry an EU energy label. Hair dryers do not have an EU energy label — please check the source. Also “Since 2021.” has a stray full stop.
issues.fix: Verify the claim and reword, e.g. refer to the power rating on the appliance or the product sheet.

issues.problem: “towel-dryiog” is a typo.
issues.fix: “towel-drying”.

issues.problem: Question “How does towel-drying save energy and time?” is copied from the hair dryer worksheet and has nothing to do with vacuum cleaners (and contains the same typo).
issues.fix: Replace with a vacuum cleaner question or remove.

issues.problem: “Since 2014., EU regulation (EU) No 666/2013regulations” — stray full stop, missing space, “regulations” repeated.
issues.fix: “Since 2014, EU Regulation (EU) No 666/2013 has capped …”.

issues.problem: “Clothe dryers”.
issues.fix: “Clothes dryers”.

issues.problem: Video title “Quick Washes v's Eco Washes”.
issues.fix: “vs” (only if it is your own text — leave it if it is the real YouTube title).

issues.problem: The “Mathematical skills” learning outcome repeats the end of the “Technical knowledge” outcome (t4d9d68a6) word for word, and ends with a stray quotation mark.
issues.fix: Write a separate mathematical-skills outcome and remove the quotation mark.

issues.problem: Bold formatting ends in the middle of the question (“… saves how** much water per flush?”).
issues.fix: Make the whole question bold, or none of it.

issues.problem: Resources line: italic starts in the middle of the formula “(*Watt × hour) / 1000 = kWh*”, and “kwh” is lower case. Same line in the computer lab worksheet.
issues.fix: “Internet, calculator and the price per kWh. *kWh = (watts × hours) / 1000*”.

issues.problem: Multiple-choice options start at “[ B ]” — the “[ A ]” in front of the first option is missing. Same in t157447ea.
issues.fix: Add “[ A ]” before the first option of both questions.

issues.problem: Heading “Microgrid Storage & Seasonal Seasonality Auditing”.
issues.fix: “Microgrid storage and seasonality”.

issues.problem: All four NL worksheets refer to “Worksheet 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, 4A, 4B”. In the new format each worksheet holds all three levels, so these numbers no longer exist (also t8f05691d, t89ea80d8, t36ed3a19, t7c1ecbfc, t6e0bd275, t2ca13c15, t2a6784ca).
issues.fix: Refer to the level instead: “see the Basic level of this worksheet”, “see the Medium level”.

issues.problem: Worked example on the break-even point ends with “they are equal only at t = 0” — correct, but there is no real break-even, which makes it a confusing example.
issues.fix: Use prices where a break-even exists (Step 4 already suggests an LED at €15).

issues.problem: “Both halve their energy roughly” — household A halves it (5 h → 2.5 h), but household B goes from 60 W to 12 W, which saves 80 %, not 50 %.
issues.fix: e.g. “Both reduce their energy use. Which approach is more robust? …”.

issues.problem: “light is OFF unless EITHER (motion is detected AND ambient light is below threshold)” — “EITHER” has no “or”.
issues.fix: “the light is OFF unless motion is detected AND the ambient light is below the threshold”.

issues.problem: Time needed “60 min – 105 - 150 (incl. walkaround)” — mixed dashes, units only on the first number.
issues.fix: “60 – 105 – 150 min (incl. walk-around)”.

issues.problem: Key-terms table: the definition “How long it takes for the savings to pay back the investment” has no term next to it.
issues.fix: Add “Payback period” in the term column.

issues.problem: “The old refrigerator and the chest freezer have the same annual consumption (438 kWh)” — the same worksheet gives the old refrigerator 730 kWh/year (200 W × 10 h × 365).
issues.fix: Compare two appliances that really have the same consumption, or correct the numbers.

issues.problem: Worked example: “Old refrigerator … already 10 years old” — the table calls the old model “15+ years”.
issues.fix: Use the same age in both places.

issues.problem: Key-terms table: definitions without a term — “Testing how conclusions change…” (Sensitivity analysis) and tf0cc387d “The number of years…” (Payback period).
issues.fix: Fill in the term column.

issues.problem: “Energy = 4.186 × 50 × 40 ÷ 3,600 ÷ 1,000 ≈ 2.3 kWh” — with the last “÷ 1,000” the result would be 0.0023 kWh. 4.186 × 50 × 40 ÷ 3,600 is already 2.3 kWh.
issues.fix: Remove “÷ 1,000”.

issues.problem: Quick programme is “45–60 °C” in the text but “55 °C” in the table (t032ec00c).
issues.fix: Say “typically 45–60 °C; this machine: 55 °C”, or use one value.

issues.problem: Upgrade B: “Replace ceramic hobs with induction” — but the cafeteria table (t41ab1528) already lists induction hobs.
issues.fix: Make the table list ceramic hobs, or change upgrade B.

issues.problem: Theory example uses a 2,000 W oven; the appliance table uses 2,200 W.
issues.fix: Use the same oven in both, or say they are different ovens.

issues.problem: Abbreviations TYH, YEC and TAC (also t454b03c1, t6d7bb22a) are never explained, and they do not translate well.
issues.fix: Write them out: “Hours per year = 5 × 365 = …”, “Energy per year = …”, “Cost per year = …”.
